I am 69 years old, I went to primary school, and I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I learned everything from my father and from watching what works on my neighbors' fields. My main land — 2 mu — runs the cabbage-chili-cabbage system, just like most people around here. The other 3 mu I split between cucumber, eggplant, and kidney bean, one mu each. I buy hybrid seeds for cabbage, cucumber, eggplant, and chili from the seed dealer in town because that is what everyone uses now and they give better yield than the old seeds. For kidney bean I buy improved seeds — no need for the most expensive kind. 

For fertilizer, I use 15-15-15 compound fertilizer and urea. I do not trust new products unless I saw them work on Old Wang's field first. On cabbage, I put one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress with half a bag of urea. That gives about 24 kilograms of nitrogen per mu. I do the same for autumn cabbage. Chili needs more potassium or the peppers stay small, so I give it one bag of compound and one bag of urea per mu, about 28 kilograms nitrogen and 14 kilograms potassium. Cucumber eats the most — one and a half bags of compound plus one bag of urea, about 32 kilograms nitrogen per mu. Eggplant gets about the same as chili. Kidney bean does not need as much nitrogen because it fixes some itself, so I only use half a bag of compound and a little urea, about 16 kilograms nitrogen per mu. I would rather put a bit too much than too little — a bad harvest is a disaster, but wasting some fertilizer is just money out of pocket. 

I irrigate from my well. Cabbage gets 3 to 4 times, chili 5 times in the hot months, cucumber 6 times because it is thirsty, eggplant 5 times, and kidney bean 3 times. I spray pesticide 2 times for cabbage and kidney bean, 4 times for chili, cucumber, and eggplant because the insects get bad in summer. I rotary till every plot before planting — that is the only practical way on my land. My family has 6 people but some work off-farm, so I do most of the labor myself. I watch my costs carefully: every yuan spent on fertilizer is a yuan less for pesticide or hired help, but I cannot afford to lose yield.
